start.yourVideoIsOn: Your video is on the timeline. To have me work on what is said, transcribe it first (Transcribe, on the video below). Tell me what you want:
start.theFinalFormatLandscape: - the **final format** (landscape, vertical 9:16, square) and the target **length**;
start.whatToCutSilences: - what to **cut**: silences, hesitations, specific passages;
start.theStyleOfCaptions: - the **style** of captions and titles, the **words to highlight**;
start.iWillShowYou: I will show you each change as a preview before applying it.
start.sourcesAreIn: Your {n} sources are in the project. For me to read what is said in the videos and sounds, transcribe them first (Transcribe, on each one in the material). Here is how I will work:
start.sourcesReadAll: - I read **everything**: the documents page by page, the pictures, the videos and sounds with what is said;
start.sourcesBrief: - what I learn goes into the project's **brief**: subject, audience, key messages, figures, brand colours;
start.sourcesDirections: - then I propose **two or three directions** for the video (format, length, scene by scene), and make the one you choose.
start.sourcesSend: The analysis is ready below: send it as it is, or add what the video is for (where it will be shown, for whom, how long).
start.kitApplied: The project's kit (brief.json) is in: its colours and fonts are the project's, and its brief is the one I follow.

assistant.itReadsTheDocument: It reads the document, renders frames to check its work and, when needed, writes new nodes for the project. It never changes anything without your approval.
assistant.forClaudeTwoPaths: For Claude, two paths: the **local companion** (your Claude Code login, no key), or the server's key. The local models' address is set here too. The badge in the header shows which path is used.
assistant.claudeOpusForThe: Claude: Opus for the most careful work, Sonnet for a good balance, Haiku to go fast. The menu also offers the **OpenAI**, **Gemini** and **OpenRouter** models the server has a key for, and **local models** (Ollama, LM Studio). You can switch models during a conversation.
assistant.justWriteWhatYou: Just write what you want. "this", "this layer", "here" refer to the **selection** and the **current time**, shown under the field.
assistant.itsChangesArriveAs: Its changes arrive as a **proposal**: visible in the preview, to apply or decline. Once applied, they can be undone like any other change.
assistant.eachConversationStaysIn: Each conversation stays in the project. Reopen one to continue it; **+** starts another without erasing the previous ones.

drawn.anImageSequencePlays: An **image sequence** plays your drawings one after another, like a cartoon. You draw in your usual software, Tramme handles the rhythm.
drawn.dropThemHereTogether: Drop them here together, numbered in their names (eye_01.png, eye_02.png…). They go into a folder named after them.
drawn.rightClickOneOf: Right-click one of the drawings, **Animate the folder**: an Image sequence layer is created with all the drawings, in order.
drawn.hold2GivesThe:
**Hold**: 2 gives the anime rhythm "on twos" (each drawing held for two frames).
**Exposure sheet**: the order and length of each drawing, for example "1-4/2, 5/6, 4-1/2, x/3".
**Forced drawing**: pick the drawing with hold keyframes, for a mouth for example.
drawn.playWithSpaceThe: Play with **Space**. The preview shows exactly the export's frames, and motion blur never blends two drawings.

sound.libraryToolsLayersMix: The sound library, the sound tools, sound layers, the mix.
sound.everySoundIsA: Every sound is a file played by a **Sound** layer. Tramme ships a library of **421 recorded sounds** (impacts, interface, digital, jingles, sci-fi; free for any use) and **sounds written as code** (whoosh, riser, boom, sparkle…). The preview and every export mix them the same way.
sound.writeSoundDesignOr: Write **/sound-design**, or simply "a whoosh on each transition". The assistant searches the library, places each sound so its **hit lands on the frame**, writes the ones the library lacks, lowers the music under a voice and checks the mix. As always, it arrives as a proposal.
sound.typeSfxToSearch: **/sfx** searches the library ("metal hit", "riser", "click"), then places a sound **on** moments the video names: entrances, exits, markers, cuts, beats, bars. Also: **/synth** (a sound written as code), **/duck** (music under the voice), **/sound-keep** (keep a sound in your library, shared by your projects), **/generate-sound** (a sound effect, a music bed or a voice-over made by a provider, when the server has a key).
sound.itsBarStartsWhere: Its bar starts where the sound plays: move it, trim it like any layer. A sound placed several times alternates its variants, so it does not sound copied.
sound.volumeAnimateItFor:
**Volume**: animate it with keyframes for a fade or to lower the sound under a voice.
**Fade in**, **Fade out**: soft starts and ends.
**Low cut**, **High cut**: thinner, or muffled and far away.
**Reverb**: the sound in a room.
**Speed**: lower and longer under 1, higher and shorter over 1.
sound.playWithSpaceThe: Play with **Space**: you hear the mix of the export. **/check** also reads the sound: a mix that clips, one far too loud or too quiet, two sounds landing together.
sound.mp4AndWebmCarry: MP4 and WebM carry the sound; **WAV** gives the sound alone, to finish it elsewhere.

editor.theEditorSPanels: The editor's panels and what they are for.
editor.everythingYouDoHere: Everything you do here changes the project's document, saved automatically. Every action can be undone with **Ctrl+Z**.
editor.theSameEngineAs: The same engine as the export. Click a layer to select it, then move, rotate or scale it with the handles. **Ctrl+wheel** to zoom, **Space** drag to pan.
editor.thePreviewCanLighten: The preview can lighten during playback depending on your computer. Here, and in the settings, you choose how far. Exports always stay at full quality.
editor.dragToReorderOr: Drag to reorder or group, double-click to rename, right-click for the rest (duplicate, precompose, hide). The **+** button adds a layer: shape, text, image, drawing sequence, particles, shader…
editor.importImagesFontsSounds: Import images, fonts, sounds and videos by drag and drop. Numbered drawings (eye_01.png, eye_02.png…) imported together go into their own folder: right-click, **Animate the folder**.
editor.spaceToPlayOr: **Space** to play or stop, arrows to step frame by frame. The timecode can be edited directly (8.5 s, 255f…).
editor.moveOrTrimThe: Move or trim the layer bars, drag the keys to change their moment. The right click opens the timeline's menus: split a clip at the playhead, a marker, the curve of a key.
editor.valuesOverTimeWith: Values over time, with their Bézier handles. This is where you tune the rhythm of a motion.
editor.thePropertiesOfThe: The properties of the selected layer, or of the composition. Each can be **static**, **animated**, an **expression** or **linked** to another (⋯ button). Modifiers and effects stack here too.
editor.askForAChange: Ask for a change: it works on the selection and the current time, checks its work with rendered frames and **proposes** its changes. You see them in the preview, then apply or decline them.
editor.mp4WebmWithTransparency: MP4, WebM with transparency, GIF, PNG sequence, Lottie, SVG or sound. The file is saved to your computer or kept in the project.
editor.moreToursAreHere: More tours are here: drawn animation, the assistant. Enjoy creating.

home.createOpenAndFind: Create, open and find your projects.
home.trammeIsAMotion:
Tramme makes motion design films from your words: you direct, it stages, builds and reviews. Every film stays a **document** you can open up and refine, in words or by hand.
This tour takes a minute.
home.mostRecentFirstWith: Most recent first, with their thumbnail. Each card's menu lets you rename, duplicate, save the .tramme archive to your computer or delete.
home.eachExampleBecomesYour: Each example becomes your own copy, which you can change freely.
home.themePreviewQualityFor: Theme, preview quality for your computer's power, access to the assistant. Shortcut: **Ctrl+,**
home.allGuidedToursAre: All guided tours are here, at any time. Another one awaits you the first time you open a project.
home.describeTheFilm: Describe the film you want, add its material (documents, pictures, footage, a whole folder), pick a format: the project opens in the studio with Tramme already at work. A blank project, a video or a file to open: **Other ways in**.

studio.title: Discover the studio
studio.summary: Direct the film in words: notes, scenes, takes.
studio.introBody:
Here you direct the film in words: Tramme stages it, builds it, reviews it. Nothing to operate.
This tour takes a minute.
studio.directBody: Say what you want, as you would to an editor: "the intro drags", "a bolder title here". **Enter** sends. **/** opens the tools and workflows.
studio.pinBody: A click on the picture pins your note there: it is about what shows at that moment. The pin (**P**) does the same.
studio.storyboardBody: Click a scene to put it in focus: your notes and the suggestions are about it. Drag to run through the film.
studio.notesBody: Each note gets a take: compare it with before, keep it, set it aside or ask for another. Everything can be undone.
studio.directionBody: What Tramme follows: the idea of the film, the brief (subject, tone, rules), the palette, the material. Correct it here: it wins over Tramme's habits.
studio.atelierBody: For the detail: layers, timeline, curves and inspector. The same project, seen up close.

tips.featuresThatDoNot: The features that do not jump out: timeline zoom, lasso, cuts, menus, fields, keyboard
tips.littleGesturesHidden: A few gestures hide in the panels. One pass, and the atelier holds no surprise any more.
tips.ctrlOrCmdAnd: **Ctrl** (or **Cmd**) and the wheel zoom the timeline around the pointer. Drag in an empty place to draw a lasso over clips and keyframes: **Shift** adds to the selection, **Ctrl** flips it.
tips.aClipsEdgesMagnetise: A clip's edges snap to the start and the end, the playhead, the markers and the other clips. Hold **Shift** to move freely.
tips.dragTheLeftEdge: Drag the left edge of a video, a sound or a composition: its head is cut off, what follows stays in place. The right edge cuts the tail.
tips.theCutInTheFile: **Cut in the file** shows the whole video and the part the layer plays. Slide the left handle to take the passage further in the file, the right one to lengthen or shorten it.
tips.thumbsAlongTheVideoClips: A video's clip shows its film: small thumbs decoded in the background, never while the film plays. The top corners of a video or a sound drag its **fade in** and **fade out**. The right click on a clip adds two tricks: a **crossfade** with the layer under it, and **loop the section to the end**.
tips.everyLineBetween: Every line between two panels drags: this one grows or shrinks the **chat**, the one over the timeline sets its height, the ones at the sides set the panels' width. Each remembers its size.
tips.theSpeedOfAVideo: A video has a **Speed** (0.25× to 4×): slower or faster, the pitch of its sound with it. Its section can also **loop** while the layer runs.
tips.rightClickTheTimeline: The timeline has its own menus. On a clip: **split**, cut the start or the end, or bring it **to the playhead**, then everything a layer can do. On an empty place or the ruler: the playhead or a **marker** there, end the composition there. On a keyframe: its curve.
tips.dragAPropertysLabel: Drag a property's name left and right to change its value. A field takes arithmetic: type **1920/2**, it is computed.
tips.theDotsOfAProperty: The diamond at the left of a property animates it (a keyframe at the playhead). The **...** at its right turn it into an expression, link it to another property or add a modifier (wiggle, loop).
tips.theWheelZoomsThe: **Ctrl** and the wheel zoom the preview, the middle button (or **Space** held) pans it. The zoom menu brings it back to fit.
tips.spacePlaysThe: **Space** plays, the arrows go one frame (with **Shift**, one second), **Home** and **End** go to the ends. **M** drops a marker, **1** to **9** jump to the markers. **Ctrl+D** duplicates, **Delete** removes.
tips.theTwoArrowsUndo: The two arrows undo and redo (**Ctrl+Z**, **Ctrl+Shift+Z**), the assistant's changes as well: their tooltip says what they undo.
tips.theClockBesideTheSaved: The clock beside the save state keeps **versions**: an instant of the project named with a date. Come back to one when a direction turned out wrong; add one before a big change.
tips.motionBlurFollowsThe: The motion blur follows the document's setting; the export can render it finer, or without blur for a quick check. When the content ends before the composition, the export offers to trim it.
tips.everythingElseExplains: Everything else explains itself: hover a control to read what it does. The other tours are under the help button.

speech.title: Speech and transcription
speech.summary: Transcribe what is said, for the captions and the assistant
speech.introBody: A sound or a video is never transcribed on its own: you decide. Once transcribed, its words are timed, ready for the captions and for the assistant, which can then cut silences or place a word at the moment it is said.
speech.materialBody: Each video and sound of the film has its **Transcribe** button here. It turns to **Transcribed** once done.
speech.inspectorBody: A sound or video layer has a **Speech** section: transcribe it, or again after a change of file.
speech.assetsBody: The sounds and videos of the project show their state here, with the button; the right click offers it too.
speech.filesBody: A sound or a video joined to a message carries the same button. When the assistant needs the words of a media not transcribed yet, it asks you first.
speech.wordsBody: Ask for captions, cuts of the silences and hesitations, or a keyword when it is said: the assistant works on the transcript.

settings.playProxiesHint: a video with a proxy (the proxy tool) plays its lighter copy here; the exports always use the original
settings.adaptsToTheMachine: Adapts to the machine: smaller if playback slows down, larger when there is room.
settings.alwaysTheStillResolution: Always the still resolution. For a powerful machine.
settings.quarterOfTheStill: Quarter of the still resolution. The lightest.
settings.theSizeOfThe: The size of the image on screen: sharp with no wasted work.
settings.alwaysTheCompositionS: Always the composition's size, even when shown smaller.
settings.theDocumentSSetting: The document's setting, as in the export.
settings.atMost4Sub: At most 4 sub-frames: close to the result, lighter.
settings.noMotionBlurIn: No motion blur in the preview (the export keeps it).
settings.automaticTheBrowserS: Automatic: the browser's (French, otherwise English). The page reloads to apply it.
settings.settingsForThisComputer: Settings for this computer, kept in this browser. Exports always render at full quality, whatever is chosen here.
settings.appearanceHint: How the editor looks in this browser: its language, its colours and the view it opens in.
settings.soundHint: How the editor plays the sound, and how the assistant places sound effects, music and voice-overs, paid ones included.
settings.picturesHint: What the assistant and the / menu use when they have a picture made and the ask names nothing. A picture made by a provider costs money: it is asked first, as for the sounds.
settings.pictureProviderHint: Automatic: the first one connected that draws (OpenAI, Gemini, Z.AI, Hydracept). Only OpenAI and Gemini change an existing picture.
settings.pictureQualityHint: Low costs less: a draft, a texture. The assistant picks per picture in automatic.
settings.pictureSizeHint: Small asks the provider's cheapest size; the upscale tool brings a picture to the frame's size afterwards.
settings.videosHint: What the assistant and the / menu use when they have a clip made and the ask names nothing. A clip made by a provider costs money: it is asked first, and each second is billed.
settings.videoProviderHint: Automatic: the first one connected that makes clips. Hydracept runs Veo 3.1 Fast.
settings.videoSecondsHint: Veo makes 4, 6 or 8 second clips; the tool can ask for another length per clip.
settings.toursHint: Short walks through the editor, offered the first time a screen opens.
settings.storageHint: The projects of this app, kept as folders on this computer.
settings.modelHint: The AI the assistant thinks with, and how hard it works on each message.
settings.behaviorHint: What the assistant does on its own: telling you it is done, starting again after a network failure, applying its changes.
settings.connectionHint: The companion runs on this computer: the assistant uses your Claude Code login through it, rather than a key.
settings.scrubAudioHint: Dragging the playhead plays a short window of the sound at each step, enough to hear the moment a cut or a hit lands. The videos' own sound is not scrubbed.
settings.likeTheExport24: Like the export: 24 frames per second for a 24 fps composition, rather than one at every screen refresh. Lighter, with no loss.
settings.sandboxPreview: Draw the preview in the plugin sandbox (experimental)
settings.sandboxPreviewHint: The whole picture, built-ins and plugins alike: modifiers, effects and simulations are evaluated and drawn in the project's worker, so a plugin's draw, tools and checks never run in the page. Video frames are still decoded here; scrubbing may show the previous picture for a moment.
settings.previewRenderStillWhen: Preview render: {still} when still, {motion} in motion (adjusted during playback).
settings.previewRenderStillWhenStill: Preview render: {still} when still, {motion} in motion.
settings.theFirstTimeThe: The first time the home screen or a project opens. All of them stay in the help menu (?).
settings.claudeOpusForThe: Claude (Opus for the most careful work, Haiku to go fast), or an OpenAI, Gemini, OpenRouter or local model.
settings.projectsFolderHint: Where this app keeps the projects, on this computer.
settings.previewVolumeHint: What you hear while playing in the editor. The exports keep the mix as it is.
settings.previewMutedHint: Plays without sound; the exports keep theirs.
settings.effectsDbHint: The level of the sound effects the assistant and the / tools place, under a voice or a music.
settings.musicDbHint: The level of a music bed made by a provider.
settings.duckDbHint: How much a music or an ambience drops while someone speaks (/duck).
settings.varySoundsHint: A sound placed on several moments alternates its variants, so it does not sound copied.
settings.confirmPaidHint: A sound effect, a music, a voice-over or a picture made by a provider costs money: you say yes first. When the assistant applies its changes by itself, the allowance below counts instead.
settings.paidPerTurn: Paid generations per turn on its own
settings.paidPerTurnHint: When the assistant applies its changes by itself, nothing is asked: a turn makes at most this many paid generations (sounds, pictures, or seconds of clips), then falls back on the library.
settings.voiceOverHint: The provider and the voice used unless the request names others (Gemini: Kore, Puck…; OpenAI: alloy, coral…; ElevenLabs: a voice id, or choose one below).
settings.voiceModelHint: Eleven v4 and v3 follow how a line is said, accent included (the Style of a voice-over). Multilingual v2 is the steadiest on long texts, Flash the cheapest.
settings.voicePickerHint: The voices of the provider above: the account's and the shared library's for ElevenLabs. Listen, then use one.
settings.soundLibraryEmpty: Empty: keep a sound there with /sound-keep.
settings.effortHint: How hard the chosen model works on each message: deeper thinking and more checks as it rises, but slower and costlier. Kept for each model. Claude: High by default, which suits most work.
settings.effortNone: This model has no effort levels.
settings.notifyDone: Tell me when the assistant is done
settings.resume: Go on after a network failure
settings.resumeHint: A task cut by the network or a busy server starts again by itself, waiting longer each time (2 s to 1 min, 6 attempts). Never after a used-up quota or a refused key.
settings.cacheTtlHint: How long Claude keeps the conversation ready, through the server's key. 5 minutes is the cheapest to write; an hour costs more to write and less when you come back after more than five minutes.
settings.notifyHint: A notification from the system when the editor is in the background (the browser asks once), a message in the editor after a long task.
settings.notifyBlocked: The browser blocks the notifications: a message in the editor after a long task only.
settings.autoApplyHint: Off: each proposal waits for your answer. When done: applied when the assistant finishes its turn. As they come: applied as soon as it makes them, the document moves while it works. Each one stays in the conversation and in the history (Ctrl+Z).
settings.autoApplyConfirm: The assistant will change the document without asking you first. Its changes are still checked before they are applied, shown in the conversation and undone with Ctrl+Z. Apply them automatically?
settings.automaticTheLocalCompanion: Automatic: the local companion if it answers (your Claude Code login), otherwise the server's key.
settings.providersIntro: Connect the AI the assistant talks with: one is enough. Its key is sent once to your server, which keeps it and adds it to each request: the editor never reads it back.
settings.providersIntroDesktop: Connect the AI the assistant talks with: one is enough. Its key is kept in this computer's keychain, and added to each request on its way to the provider: the editor never reads it back.
settings.noProviderConnected: No provider connected yet: add one below.
settings.serverSecretHint: Key set on the server (wrangler secret). A key added here takes its place.
settings.disconnectConfirm: Disconnect {name}? Its key is deleted from the server.
settings.keepTheKey: Leave empty to keep the current key
settings.providerAnthropic: Claude, with a key from your Anthropic account
settings.providerOpenai: GPT, ChatGPT's models, and voice-overs. A ChatGPT subscription does not include a key: it comes from the OpenAI platform, billed apart
settings.providerGemini: Gemini models, and voice-overs. Google AI Studio gives a key, free to start
settings.providerOpenrouter: Hundreds of models from one account
settings.providerHydracept: Pictures, sound effects, music and voice-overs with one key, a quote and a receipt for each
settings.providerCustom: Any service of the OpenAI chat format, by its base URL (DeepSeek, Groq, Mistral…)
settings.themeHint: One palette for the whole interface. System follows the computer’s light or dark setting.
settings.viewHint: The studio: you direct the film in words, Tramme stages it, builds it and reviews it. The atelier: the layers, the timeline and the inspector, for the detail. The same project either way.

timeline.noHandleLeft: The files have no handle left for this length: {missing} s missing (shorten the transition, or trim the shots)

timeline.trimStartToPlayhead: Trim the start to the playhead
timeline.trimEndToPlayhead: Trim the end from the playhead
timeline.magnetic: Magnetic track: the clips close their gaps
timeline.makeSequence: Lay the layers out on tracks
timeline.cannotPlaceHere: This clip cannot go on that track
timeline.copyChapters: Copy the chapters as a list

perception.noPulse: No steady pulse in this sound; {hits} hits found, and its loudness over time.

personal.noServiceWorker: This browser cannot keep projects here (service workers are off, often in private browsing). Open Tramme in a normal window of a recent browser.
personal.vaultUnreachable: The key vault does not answer: reload the page.
personal.viaRelay: through the Tramme relay, which keeps nothing (this provider refuses calls from a browser)
personal.keysIntro: Your keys stay in this browser, in a vault the editor and the projects' plugins cannot read. Your browser calls the provider directly; Tramme never sees a key, and the provider bills you.
personal.forgetKeysConfirm: Every key and custom provider is removed from this browser. Continue?
personal.vaultAlone: This page keeps your Tramme keys. Open Tramme to use them.
personal.storedHere: Your projects are kept in this browser, on this device only: Tramme keeps nothing. Export them (.tramme) to back them up or open them elsewhere.

sources.none: No sources in the project yet.

studio.wholeFilmHint: Your note is about the whole film. Click a scene on the storyboard to talk about it alone.
studio.momentHint: The moment your note is written at
studio.pinHint: Pin the note on the picture: click where it applies (P)
studio.pinNow: Click on the picture where your note applies
studio.placeholder: Tell Tramme what you want, as you would tell an editor…
studio.chipFillHint: Fills the bar: finish the sentence
studio.anotherTakeHint: Set this take aside and ask for another, in a different direction
studio.anotherTakePrompt: Another take of "{label}": the same intent, a clearly different direction.
studio.notesEmptyText: Write what you want in the bar under the film, as you would to an editor. Tramme stages it, builds it, reviews it, and brings you a take.
studio.notesEmptyPin: Click the picture to pin a note on what is there
studio.notesEmptyScene: Click a scene on the storyboard to talk about it alone
studio.notesEmptyTakes: Compare each take with before, keep it or ask for another
studio.inviteText: Describe it in the bar below: the subject, the tone, the length. Drop documents, pictures or footage: Tramme reads them before staging anything.
studio.makingText: Tramme is staging your film. The scenes appear here as soon as they are built.
studio.dropHint: Drop your files: they go with your next note

chips.reviewWords: Watch the whole film as an art director would and fix what matters most: readability, rhythm, hierarchy, the transitions.
chips.paceWords: Give the film more rhythm: shorten the scenes that drag, sharper entrances, cuts on the beat, without changing the message.
chips.paletteWords: Propose another palette for the film, in keeping with its subject and tone, and apply it everywhere.
chips.soundWords: Work on the sound of the film: a bed that fits the tone, effects on the moments that matter, levels balanced.
chips.verticalWords: Make a vertical 9:16 version of the film for social media, in a new composition, each scene recomposed for the format.
chips.impactWords: Make this scene hit harder: a franker entrance, more contrast, a clearer hierarchy.
chips.calmerWords: Make this scene calmer: fewer things moving, softer moves, more air around the words.
chips.layoutWords: Recompose this scene differently: another layout and another camera move, the same message.
chips.shorterWords: Shorten this scene by about a third without losing its message, and move what follows.

direction.title: Direction
direction.briefHint: What Tramme follows, over its own habits. It writes it from your material and your notes; correct it here.
direction.aboutHint: The subject, the audience, the purpose, the key messages, the facts to get right
direction.toneHint: Two or three lines on the character of the film
direction.rulesHint: One per line: what to always do, what never to do
direction.noMaterial: No material yet. The documents, pictures, footage and sounds you add are read by Tramme before it stages anything.
direction.notSaved: The brief could not be saved: {error}

transcribe.hint: Turn what is said into timed words, for the captions and the assistant

transcribe.notYet: Not transcribed. Transcribe it to place captions on the words and let the assistant read what is said.
transcribe.readyHint: Transcribed: the captions and the assistant can use the words.
transcribe.askText: The assistant needs what is said in {name}. Transcribe it now?

removebg.done: The background of {name} is cut out.

dictation.start: Dictate: speak, then click again to write what you said
dictation.stop: Stop and write what you said
dictation.micRefused: The microphone is blocked. Allow it for Tramme in the system or browser settings.
dictation.failed: Could not write what you said: {error}
dictation.downloadText: To write what you say, Tramme runs {model} on this computer ({size}, downloaded once). Your voice stays on this computer.

localModels.title: Models
localModels.hint: The models the editor runs on this computer. Each downloads the first time its tool runs, or with its button, and stays in this browser; nothing is sent anywhere. The choice is for this computer.
localModels.ownLicence: under its own licence: read it before a commercial project
localModels.notTried: not tried with this version of Tramme
localModels.noteU2netpPerson: trained on any subject, not on people: rougher hair and edges, but it runs on the smallest machines
localModels.noteU2net: finer edges than the small one, for about forty times the download
localModels.noteIsnet: reads 1024 px: the sharpest edges and the heaviest; it may exceed the GPU of a modest machine (the processor then takes over, slowly)
localModels.noteYolosSmall: finds smaller and farther things, about four times slower
localModels.noteNonCommercial: finer depth, for non-commercial work only
localModels.noteWhisperBase: faster, more mistakes on names and accents
localModels.noteWhisperTiny: the fastest, for a first pass
localModels.noteWhisperLarge: the most accurate; best in the desktop app or with the companion
localModels.advancedHint: Any model of the model hub made for the same pipeline (transformers.js, ONNX weights): it is downloaded and tried on a blank picture or a second of silence before it is used.
localModels.hubModelHint: For detection, depth or transcription: owner/name, as on huggingface.co
localModels.notAHubId: {id} is not a model hub id (owner/name)
localModels.hubModelKept: {id} answered: it is now used for {task} on this computer
localModels.cacheHint: The models kept by this browser weigh {size} in all. Below, those no row uses (an earlier choice, an older version): delete them to free the space.
localModels.nothingElse: Nothing else: every model kept here is in use.
localModels.soundHint: The server transcribes with its own model when it has one (Workers AI, or an OpenAI key). Otherwise the local companion runs the model chosen here (TRAMME_WHISPER_MODEL on its machine overrides it), and without a companion, this browser does.
localModels.dictationHint: Where the microphone of a message box is transcribed. The downloaded model keeps your voice on this computer; the companion runs it on this computer too; the server sends it away.

components.definedNotice: {name} is a component now: its first instance is in place of the layers.

plugins.title: Plugins
plugins.hint: Installed once, offered in every project: their tools, workflows and checks run in each project's sandbox; what draws is copied into the project that uses it, so it opens anywhere.
plugins.whereDesktop: the app's folder of plugins, on this computer
plugins.notPersistentHint: It did not grant lasting storage: install Tramme as an app, and keep a backup of your plugins (below).
plugins.importHint: A .js module or a .trammeplugin package, picked or dropped here; a backup (.zip) is put back.
plugins.backupHint: Every plugin and which are off, in one file: to keep, or to bring to another device.
plugins.noneHint: Install one from a file, or keep a project's plugin here with library-add.
plugins.duplicates: Some plugins are installed twice under different files: remove the older one.
plugins.sandboxed: Its code runs only in each project's sandbox, never on the page.
plugins.newerApi: {name} needs the plugin API {api}; this Tramme has {ours}: update Tramme
plugins.onHere: Installed plugin on in this project
plugins.offHere: Installed plugin off in this project
plugins.copied: {names} copied into the project: it opens the same anywhere
plugins.stopped: {name} failed {n} times in a row: it is stopped until the editor opens again
